1
What is not a reasonable estimate of the physical property indicated?
A
2  103
W for the power dissipated by the heating element of an electric kettle
B
4  102
m3 for the volume of water in a swimming pool
C
5  105
N s for the momentum of a lorry moving along a road
D
6  102
N for the weight of a fully grown racehorse

hints: Start by translating the weight in $\text{N}$ into a mass using $W = mg$ with $g \approx 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, and compare with the mass of a large animal and a human.

Check the other three quantities with a quick order-of-magnitude calculation: $P = VI$ for the $230 \text{ V}$ kettle, length x width x depth for the pool, and $p = mv$ for a multi-tonne lorry at road speed.
Look for the estimate that is wrong by about a factor of 10: a $60 \text{ kg}$ object weighs about as much as a person, not a racehorse.
walkthrough: To test reasonableness, compare each quoted value with a quick calculation using familiar sizes, masses and speeds.
Kettle power $2 \times 10^3 \text{ W}$ matches mains heating: $P = VI \approx 230 \text{ V} \times 10 \text{ A} \approx 2.3 \times 10^3 \text{ W}$.
Pool volume $4 \times 10^2 \text{ m}^3$ matches length x width x depth, for example $25 \text{ m} \times 10 \text{ m} \times 1.6 \text{ m} = 4.0 \times 10^2 \text{ m}^3$.

Lorry momentum $5 \times 10^5 \text{ N s}$ matches $p = mv$, for example $m \approx 2 \times 10^4 \text{ kg}$ and $v \approx 25 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives $p \approx 5.0 \times 10^5 \text{ kg m s}^{-1} = 5.0 \times 10^5 \text{ N s}$.

Horse weight $6 \times 10^2 \text{ N}$ gives $m = W/g \approx 600/10 = 60 \text{ kg}$, which is about a human mass and about ten times too small for a $\approx 500 \text{ kg}$ racehorse whose weight should be $\approx 5 \times 10^3 \text{ N}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: A kettle typically draws about $10 \text{ A}$ from $230 \text{ V}$ mains, giving $P = VI \approx 2 \times 10^3 \text{ W}$, so this is reasonable.

B.explanation: A $25 \text{ m} \times 10 \text{ m} \times 2 \text{ m}$ pool has volume $\approx 5 \times 10^2 \text{ m}^3$, so $4 \times 10^2 \text{ m}^3$ is reasonable.

C.explanation: A lorry of mass $\approx 2 \times 10^4 \text{ kg}$ at $\approx 25 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ has $p = mv \approx 5 \times 10^5 \text{ N s}$, so this is reasonable.

D.explanation: Weight $6 \times 10^2 \text{ N}$ implies mass $m = W/g \approx 60 \text{ kg}$, far smaller than a fully grown racehorse of about $500 \text{ kg}$.
